summary.intent: Execute all 14 plans of GSD phase 68.1 (wiring CipherBox's web app onto the node/v3 read+write chain, replacing 46 runtime stubs) via wave-based subagent orchestration, then run successive rounds of gap-closure planning/execution driven by live e2e failures and the user's own hands-on bug reports, aiming for a fully green 208-spec web-e2e suite and WEB-01..WEB-04 sign-off.
summary.outcome: Phase 68.1 went through three full execution+verification rounds (14 → 8 → 7 → 2 gap-closure plans, 31 plans total) taking e2e failures from 202/208 down to a handful of approved deferrals (recovery.html v2-only, rotation-durability SC-4) plus flakes; found and fixed multiple real production bugs (write-plane cold-load loss, move write-link orphaning, kind-cache never wired into shared browser, wrong-key file decryption, durable IPNS registration) directly from user's manual testing, with verification round 3 and a final closing e2e run in progress when the transcript ends.

repo: CipherBox write-plane is keyed by node UUID (childId), read-plane by ipnsName (SealedChildRef) — conflating the two causes silent write-capability loss; every write-chain bug found (move, batch-upload, shared-subfolder-write, GAP-1 wrong key) was some variant of this split being threaded incorrectly.

TEE republish enrollment requires both encryptedIpnsPrivateKey AND keyEpoch on POST /ipns/publish; createFolder originally omitted this for new subfolders, so their IPNS records were never enrolled and died at TTL — durability gap distinct from routing-store volatility.

mock-ipns-routing (delegated routing on :3001) stores IPNS records in an in-memory Map wiped on every container restart; API's ipns_records DB cache only persists records that were actually published through the API, so casually restarting that container manufactures fake 'broken navigation' bugs.

docker/docker-compose.yml mock-ipns-routing healthcheck used busybox `wget localhost`, which resolves to ::1 while the app binds IPv4-only, causing perpetual false-unhealthy status; fixed to 127.0.0.1.
API listens on :3000; :3001 is the delegated-routing mock (DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL target for e2e) — easy to confuse when health-probing.

apps/web/public/recovery.html (last touched Phase 24) only accepts legacy v2 single-key vault blobs/metadata; app has produced v3/node-v3 blobs since Phase 62, so recovery flow is architecturally broken and needs its own dedicated plan, not a quick patch.

shares.item_name plaintext column was dropped entirely (not renamed) in migration 1750000000000-ApiSchemaCutover, making the REQ-4 itemName-backfill feature permanently dead code; reviving it as plaintext would violate the project's zero-knowledge rule — redesign must ride the already-partially-shipped item_name_encrypted/ECIES pipeline.

dfsFindFolder in client.ts always re-resolved/re-unsealed/overwrote every intermediate ancestor's folderTree entry on every call, contradicting its 'later calls are cheap' docstring — root cause of breadcrumb-up empty-flash bugs; fix added a cache short-circuit for already-loaded write-capable entries.

enumerateSharedSubtree was built on a share_keys per-child-key fan-out that the live API never populated (grants wrap the whole subtree with one ECIES wrap of the root readKey) — had to be rewritten as a recursive read/write-chain DFS.

SharedWriteContext has no ipnsPrivateKey field; shared-write ops derive the publish key from inside the unsealed write-body via unsealParentWriteBody, so recovering a subfolder's writeKey alone (not the private key) is sufficient to unblock deep shared writes.

git stash is prohibited across this project's worktree-isolated agents because refs/stash is shared across worktrees — at least two separate subagents accidentally ran `git stash push` mid-task and had to self-recover (one via manual reapply, one via stash pop) before committing.

Decision-coverage gate in gsd-tools parses CONTEXT.md bullets requiring the colon inside the bold group (`- **D-04 [informational]:**`); a tag placed outside the bold group is silently ignored by the parser.

code.finding: downloadFromIpns originally fed the parent folderKey into sdk-core's resolveFileMetadata (which needs the file's OWN readKey), causing 'Decryption failed' in the text editor/version history — a type coincidence (both Uint8Array) let it through silently.

moveItem originally only re-linked the read-plane SealedChildRef and left the moved child's WriteChildRef orphaned in the source write-body, permanently breaking edit/save after a move into a subfolder — fixed by unsealing under source writeKey, dropping from source, re-sealing under dest writeKey, keyed by node UUID not the ipnsName-based childId param.
targetFolder?.isLoaded fast path was verified correct (reads fresh zustand state synchronously); the actual breadcrumb-up bug lived one layer below in client.ts's dfsFindFolder.
navigateToSubfolder seeded nested shared folders with a zero writeKey, blocking all deep (non-root) shared writes — fixed via a new one-hop resolveSharedSubfolderWriteKey resolver keyed by node UUID.
hardcoded isFolder = true stub meant the D-02 kind cache (populated in 68.1-14) was never consulted in the shared browser, so files were always treated as folders there.

workflow: Long-running background e2e subagents repeatedly 'lose their wake' — they launch a background suite, end their turn to wait, and never get re-invoked when it finishes (transcript sometimes gets evicted entirely); mitigation is an independent disk-based watchdog (polling .last-run.json or similar) plus prompt-based SendMessage resume while the transcript is still warm, falling back to a fresh continuation agent with explicit completed_state when evicted.

User's live hands-on testing (headed Playwright run, manual logout/login, manual text-editor use) found real bugs that the automated e2e suite structurally could not reach because describe.serial specs abort at the first failure, hiding all coverage after that point — 'green suite' claims must be checked against how deep the serial run actually got, not just pass/fail counts.
Always verify a reported git commit failure via `git log -1` before assuming it didn't land — 1Password-integrated commit signing produces false-negative timeouts even when the commit succeeded.

When a wave executor reports a worktree's expected_base metadata, don't trust it blindly — verify the true fork point via `git merge-base` before recording, since an agent can misreport its own HEAD as the base.

Running two full 208-spec confirmation runs (baseline vs post-fix HEAD) is the way to close out a verifier's 'fixes landed after the last recorded run' complaint — a single stale artifact isn't sufficient evidence for sign-off.
